newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europe's march of the unemployed reaches Paris.
newsitem.headline: Europe's march of the unemployed reaches Paris.

text.p: A march by scores of unemployed workers reached Paris on Friday, the half-way point in a two-month "European March For Jobs" which will end in Amsterdam in mid-June.
The march, which has been coordinated with others across Europe, has a hefty French contingent and is due to reach the Dutch capital in time for a summit of EU government leaders on June 16.

The arrival of a contingent from Spain and south-eastern and south-western France coincides with the French parliamentary election campaign, where there are signs that voters are at best sceptical about the ability of the left or the right to tackle record unemployment.

At Orly airport in southern Paris, where the first of several protest meetings in the Paris region will be held before the next stage of the march, few said they would vote for any of the major political parties, left or right.

"It's not about lining up behind traditional political lines," says Yann, an unemployed French sociologist who, like his fellow-militants, wants a total departure from what he describes as tired political formulas and broken promises.

Like many of his fellow marchers, he hopes that the march will unite unemployed and marginalised people across Europe to create a wider groundswell of protest against mainstream politicians in France and across Europe.
"Our ancestors fought for three famous principles: 'Liberty, Egality, Fraternity'. I would like to add one more, 'Dignity', the right to work and the right to a roof over your head.

The "European March Against Unemployment, Precarity and Exclusion" is coordinated by unemployment activitists and poverty action groups determined fearful that European political and monetary ties are being forged with little social input.
The Amsterdam rally will unite marchers from cities across the European Union.
